details.description: GLM-5.2 is a flagship large language model from Z.ai (Zhipu AI), which its documentation describes as "a flagship model built for the era of long-horizon tasks," succeeding GLM-5.1. It is released as open weights (MIT license, per its Hugging Face model card) and is offered on Mistral AI's La Plateforme as a third-party open-weight model. GLM-5.2 has a 1-million-token context window, multiple reasoning effort levels, and tool-calling and MCP support for agentic and long-horizon coding workflows.
advantages: Scores 91.2 on GPQA-Diamond, per Z.ai's GLM-5.2 model card on Hugging Face.
Scores 99.2 on AIME 2026, per Z.ai's GLM-5.2 model card on Hugging Face.
Scores 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro and 81.0-82.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, per Z.ai's documentation.
Z.ai reports IndexShare, which reuses indexers across sparse attention layers, cuts per-token computation by 2.9x at 1-million-token context length.
Supports multiple reasoning effort levels alongside tool calling and MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for agentic workflows, per Z.ai's documentation.
disadvantages: Text-only: Z.ai's documentation and model card do not describe image or vision input support.
Scores 40.5 on Humanity's Last Exam without tool use (54.7 with tools), per its Hugging Face model card.
Z.ai's model card documents support for English and Chinese only.
use_cases: Long-horizon agentic coding and software engineering tasks
Project-scale codebase understanding and multi-step development workflows
General reasoning tasks with configurable effort levels

notes: Provider 'mistral' in the catalog reflects that Mistral AI's La Plateforme hosts this third-party open-weight model from Z.ai (Mistral's models overview lists 'Z.ai GLM 5.2' under Generalist / Open-weight models with a 1M-token context window); Z.ai is the maker, matching this entry's maker field. Catalog facts (1,048,576 input / 131,072 output tokens, text-only modality) match Z.ai's stated 1M context window and 128K max output. Total parameter count (753B) and an exact release date were not independently confirmed on a second maker page, so left out of the description beyond what both sources agreed on; no separate GitHub repository was found for this model.
